```{r}
#install.packages('mice')
library(tidyverse)
library(mice)
library(naniar)
library(brms)

tiantan <- read_csv(
  '../data/PRSA_Data_Tiantan_20130301-20170228.csv')
wanliu <- read_csv(
  '../data/PRSA_Data_Wanliu_20130301-20170228.csv')
wanshouxigong <- read_csv(
  '../data/PRSA_Data_Wanshouxigong_20130301-20170228.csv')
```

Daily average aggregation
```{r}
# Combine datasets, factor station
air_quality <- bind_rows(
  tiantan,
  wanliu,
  wanshouxigong
) |>
  mutate(
    station = as.factor(station))
```

Missingness
```{r}
# Missingness statistics
miss_var_summary(air_quality)

# Visualize missingness
vis_miss(air_quality, warn_large_data = FALSE)
```

Check correlations
```{r}
subset <- air_quality |>  select(
    PM2.5, TEMP, DEWP, WSPM,
    PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, 
    O3, PRES, RAIN
  )

corr_matrix <- round(cor(subset, use = 'complete.obs'), 2)

corrplot(
  corr_matrix,
  method = 'ellipse',
  type = 'lower',
  addCoef.col = 'black',
  number.cex = .7
)
```

Suppose MAR, random streaks of missing observations across rows. We impute hourly observations first, then aggregate to daily averages.
```{r}
# Prepare hourly data, select variables of interest
imputed_data <- air_quality |>
  select(
    year, month, day, hour,
    PM2.5, TEMP, DEWP, WSPM,
    station, PM10, NO2, SO2, CO,
    O3, PRES, RAIN
  )

# Generate predictor matrix using quickpred()
pred <- quickpred(
  imputed_data,
  mincor = 0.1,
  minpuc = 0.25
)

# Ensure date/time and station variables predict air quality variables
pred[
  c("PM2.5", "TEMP", "DEWP", "WSPM",
    "PM10", "NO2", "SO2", "CO", "O3", "PRES", "RAIN"),
  c("year", "month", "day", "hour", "station")
] <- 1

# No variable predicts itself
diag(pred) <- 0

# Do not impute date/time or station variables
# meth default for numerical variables is predictive mean matching (pmm)
meth <- make.method(imputed_data)

meth[c("year", "month", "day", "hour", "station")] <- ""

# Run MICE pmm imputation
imp <- mice(
  imputed_data,
  m = 1,
  maxit = 10,
  predictorMatrix = pred,
  method = meth,
  seed = 123
)

# Extract
complete_imp <- complete(imp, 1)

# Aggregate into daily averages
complete_imp <- complete_imp |>
  mutate(
    date = as.Date(sprintf(
      "%04d-%02d-%02d", year, month, day
    ))
  ) |>
  group_by(station, date) |>
  summarise(
    across(
      c(PM2.5, TEMP, DEWP, WSPM,
        PM10, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, PRES, RAIN),
      mean
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Save as a single csv file
write_csv(complete_imp, file = '../data/imputed_data.csv')
```

Note that because we are using m = 1 (creating only one imputed dataset), the subsequent Bayesian HMC analysis will not incorporate uncertainty between multiple imputed datasets. Also, standard MICE does not explicitly model temporal autocorrelation.
